findings.summary: Security-adversary (verdict EXPOSED): run_holdout forwarded user args unchecked and argparse takes the LAST --form, so `holdout run --vault <url> --form all` cloned the private vault and ran its bodies through the DEV printer — emitting the plant text, both oracle regexes, and 1500 chars of raw verifier output per body. The egress tests were green because they seeded holdout=True by hand (the inert-control shape). Pre-existing hole, inherited and widened by this span (diagnose forwards the same way).
findings.disposition: run_holdout now REFUSES any forwarded --form before cloning anything (ValueError naming the exposure). Regression pinned in the plugins suite so closure is mechanical, plus a harness twin in _holdout_adversary_fold_tests.

findings.summary: Security-adversary: judge_control ran the opus judge with cwd=calibration/ inside the public working tree; the sandbox profile re-grants file-write to its workspace, so the ONE model holding approved bodies + oracle regexes in context (fed adversary-authored text — the injection shape) had OS-level write access to the directory that gets committed and pushed, with network allowed.
findings.disposition: The judge now runs in a throwaway tdd-judge- temp dir deleted after each rep; the vault deny-read forwarding is asserted through the dispatch (a **kw double can no longer let it vanish). Network-deny remains the standing deferred B3 item (two-tier plan), unchanged in scope by this fix.

findings.summary: Security-adversary: the plan required no-TTY -> ABORT for the judge's transient rationale (it quotes the oracle), but the guard landed only on remediate — a refused `holdout approve` from CI/an agent's Bash tool/`| tee` would have written oracle regexes into a durable log or the ~/.claude transcript pile. The custody test could not see it because its denominator was the vault directory only.
findings.disposition: Approve's judge dispatch is now TTY-gated exactly like remediate (non-interactive prints 'judge skipped', the deterministic refusal stands alone); injectable `interactive` for tests. Harness: test_harness.py::_control_judge_tests 'JUDGE SEC3' (calibration/ is a fixed gate stage, so `incorporated` with the harness cite per the repo's closure-evidence constraint).

findings.summary: Integration-adversary GAP5, confirmed live by a red-first test before the fix: cmd_remediate_holdout branched only on `approvable`, so an INCONCLUSIVE control (every rep an environment failure — zero measured) fell into the judge-and-retire path with empty reasoning; an irreversible corpus transition could ride a run that measured nothing, breaking D1's own fail-closed rule. Caught in-span, never shipped.
findings.disposition: inconclusive now short-circuits before any judge spend or disposition ('nothing was measured, nothing is judged or retired'). Harness: _remediation_tests 'D4 GAP5' proves the judge is never called and statuses stay untouched.

findings.summary: Integration-adversary ISLAND1 (+ arch-F6): the persisted validation manifest had exactly one writer and zero readers, and vault_integrity_problems could not distinguish a D1-gated body from one hand-copied beside a hand-written register row — the approve gate was walk-aroundable and the registry's named consumer pointed back at the writer (the H11 shape).
findings.disposition: vault_integrity_problems now REQUIRES, for every CURRENT body registered on/after 2026-08-17, a manifest whose candidate_content_sha256 matches the body (missing or stale -> integrity problem; pre-gate bodies grandfathered by register date — their cleanup is the D4 sweep). contract_mismatch_warnings additionally reads each manifest's model/isolation against the launching run (the plan's risk-3 'reporting flags a mismatch', now real). Harness: _remediation_tests ISLAND1 trio + _holdout_adversary_fold_tests ARCH-F1 pair.

findings.summary: Integration-adversary ISLAND2 (+ arch-F7/F8): the per-run population snapshot was written and read by nothing — the 'old blocks interpreted with as-of-then status' purpose had no implementing consumer, and plant_vitality/ledger reinterpret history status-blind (a retired body keeps accruing streaks and can spend a prediction).
findings.disposition: Two real readers now exist: holdout_summary_lines prints as-of-run population counts, and history_format.reading_of is the safe corrected-first accessor (arch-F7); the parsed key renamed population_snapshot to stop colliding with population_of (arch-F8); unknown statuses parse as visible 'unparseable', never a silent drop (arch-F3). The still-blind readers (vitality streaks, ledger binder) are OWNED DATED DEBT: capabilities.json holdout-control-validation/population-snapshot-consumers, david, expires 2026-11-15, expiry proven by validate --as-of.

findings.summary: Architecture-adversary F1 (gate-by-proxy): approve/validate defaulted to 'sonnet' while the eval defaults to 'haiku', so on the default path the gate certified a control k/k against a model the reading never uses — 'the contract MUST equal the eval contract' was enforced only by help text.
findings.disposition: ONE model default (rc.DEFAULT_MODEL) used by the eval argparse and all four holdout gate sites; contract_mismatch_warnings prints a CONTRACT MISMATCH line (ids only) whenever a manifest's recorded model/isolation differs from the run being launched. Harness: _holdout_adversary_fold_tests ARCH-F1 checks both directions.

findings.summary: Architecture-adversary F2/F3/F4/F5/F9 (verdict MIXED(9)) — five duplication/reuse misses, none yet divergent but each the documented shape that diverges later: a second rep loop in validate_item; the status vocabulary re-spelled in a regex and a second EXCLUDED literal; four copies of latest-row-wins; the legacy recall/fp arithmetic duplicated beside partition_readings; a private bodies loader + a twin file-sha helper on either side of the TOCTOU comparison.
findings.disposition: All five collapsed to single owners: rc.run_reps/rep_counts shared by eval and gate; EXCLUDED_STATUSES lives beside VALID_STATUS with a membership assert and _POP_ITEM derives from it; plant_forms.resolve_latest is the one fold (resolve_forms/resolve_statuses/holdout CAS all derive); legacy reading = partition_readings(results, {}); remediate uses rc.load_corpus and plant_forms.plant_sha replaces _sha256_file (the TOCTOU comparison now compares one implementation with itself). Harness 572/572 green across the refactor.

findings.summary: Test-quality adversary (verdict HOLLOW(7)), proven by mutation: every approve/remediate/validate test injected a validator double, so replacing the `if validator is None` default with an approve-everything stub survived all 130 holdout checks — the single sentence D1 exists to guarantee ('no body lands until its verifier actually ran') was the one thing the suite did not test. Also: a literal-True check, a tautological D3 check, an immutability check asserting only file existence, an untested cmd_validate_holdout, and judge doubles that discarded **kw (the deny_read could vanish unseen).
findings.disposition: DEFAULT-WIRE tests drive cmd_approve_holdout and cmd_validate_holdout with NO injected validator against stub binaries, both directions (missed plant refuses to land; caught plant lands) — the mutation cannot survive. deny_read asserted through both judge dispatch paths; byte-identical immutability assert; the literal-True check now asserts agent_coverage_problems; the tautological D3 check now fails on the regression it names. The macOS-only gating of live-spawn tests (sandbox-exec) remains — recorded below as a limitation, not silently.

findings.summary: Tripwire-auditor (6/7 + FLOWS 4/4): the plan's actual D4 outcome — the real private vault remediated, diagnose re-run, both readings reported — was deferred to David in PROSE ONLY (README + an end-of-run tip), with no dated mechanical trigger; if never run, the corpus keeps its broken controls and the holdout FP number keeps measuring authoring quality silently — the exact failure the plan exists to end (the H7 prose-deferral shape).
findings.disposition: Dated integration_debt holdout-corpus-remediation-sweep (owner david, expires 2026-09-30) added; `capability_registry.py validate --as-of 2026-10-01` exits 1 naming it, and test_own_registry runs validate on the REAL clock every suite run, so the lapse REDs the suite mechanically. The sweep itself is interactive-only BY DESIGN (the y/n half cannot be automated) — the parking is now LEGITIMATE, not dark.

findings.summary: Tripwire-auditor + test-quality adversary, recorded rather than fixed: the end-to-end flow tests that spawn a (stub) binary under holdout confinement — the D0 register->scorer subprocess flow and the DEFAULT-WIRE approve tests — gate on sandbox_exec_available() and emit a visible SKIPPED-ok on Linux, so the ubuntu CI re-run never exercises them; their green is the author's macOS only. Structurally forced: holdout runs fail closed without sandbox-exec by design (the same reason the holdout eval itself is Mac-only), and the partition/gate LOGIC is covered cross-platform by pure-function tests.
findings.disposition: Accepted as a stated limitation matching the repo's existing sandbox-gating precedent (two-tier part 2's CI-RED lesson); the SKIPPED lines are explicit in output. Revisit only if a Linux confinement path (the deferred Docker/API-key lane) ever lands.
